verdict.rationale: Windmill documents its own programmatic path for creating and updating flows: flows can be defined in YAML or as code, deployed through the `wmill` CLI from a Git repository, and auto-deployed from new commits via Git sync. An agent could plausibly drive that path. However, nothing in the pack documents a public REST API endpoint for creating, updating, or activating flows, and the OpenAPI probe returned 404 on every candidate path. The MCP docs only cover triggering existing scripts and flows. Missing for 10: documented public API endpoints for flow create/update, an explicit activation/enable step, any agent-driven example, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent create, update, and activate a workflow programmatically through the public API

citations.quote: An orchestrator for assembling these functions into efficient, low-latency flows, using either a low-code builder or YAML
as well as CLI deployments from a Git repository
Windmill can automatically deploy new commits from the repository into the workspace
